title: Ashtpadi 23, salok: the ointment of wisdom
hook: giaan anjan gur deeaa: the Guru gave the ointment of wisdom and the darkness went (Sukhmani 23)

segments.voice: Yesterday, jeea, and your line: everything alive is his. Did something neglected get a moment of care? Today the twenty-third ashtpadi begins, and it starts with the eyes. Day five hundred twenty-six.

In many Punjabi homes, there's a small bottle or a little metal pot of surma, a fine dark powder for the eyes. A grandmother might line a baby's eyes with it, or her own, with a thin stick, an old custom across South Asia. People say it cools the eyes and protects them. Gurbani's word for eye-ointment like this is anjan. And the twenty-third ashtpadi of Sukhmani opens with the Guru putting anjan on someone's eyes.
screen: `A LITTLE POT OF SURMA.` → `LINED WITH A THIN STICK.` → `ANJAN, FROM THE GURU.`

segments.voice: The salok, in paraphrase: the Guru gave the ointment of spiritual wisdom, and the darkness of ignorance was destroyed. By God's grace I met the holy one, and Nanak's mind was lit up. Take it in pieces. Giaan is wisdom, knowledge, especially the kind that knows God. Anjan is the eye-ointment, the kohl or surma. So giaan anjan is wisdom pictured as a balm for the eyes. And notice who applies it: the Guru, gur deeaa, the Guru gave it. You don't put it on yourself. Then the result: agiaan andher binaas. Agiaan is the opposite of giaan, not-knowing. Andher is darkness. Binaas means destroyed, gone. The darkness isn't argued away; it simply ends, the way a dark room ends when someone opens the shutters. The second line adds how it happened: har kirpaa, by God's grace, the seeker met the holy one. And the last word is pargaas: light, illumination, the mind lit from within. Look at what ointment actually does. Ointment doesn't add anything new to the world. The trees, the faces, the sky were all there already. It just lets you see them. That's how Sikh teaching often talks about the Guru's wisdom: not as information piled on top of life, but as clearer eyes for the life that's already in front of you. Over the next days, the twenty-third ashtpadi will show what those cleared eyes see.
screen: `GIAAN ANJAN: WISDOM AS EYE-BALM.` · `GUR DEEAA: THE GURU APPLIES IT.` · `THE DARKNESS ENDS, LIKE SHUTTERS OPENING.` · `NOT NEW THINGS: CLEARER EYES.` · then, large: `THE GURU CLEARED MY EYES.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: wash your eyes with cool water. If you can, go to a sink. Cup cool water in your hands and bring it gently to your closed eyes, two or three times. Dry them slowly. Then sit, eyes closed, and feel the coolness fade. When you're ready, open them slowly, and let the first thing you see simply be there. If you pray, you can say Waheguru as you open your eyes. The bell holds the time.
Giaan anjan, the eye-ointment of wisdom: the Guru gave it, and the darkness of ignorance was gone.
Your line: the guru cleared my eyes. Today, before you judge a situation, take one breath and look at it again, as if with cleared eyes. Day five hundred twenty-six.

howItsDone: Sikhs reciting Sukhmani Sahib's twenty-third ashtpadi begin with a salok picturing the Guru's wisdom as anjan, eye-ointment, that ends the darkness of ignorance.

myth: in the salok, the seeker applies the ointment alone
gur deeaa: the Guru gave it.
anjan is the same kind of eye-ointment as surma or kohl
a dark powder used across South Asia, said to cool and protect the eyes.
the salok says wisdom adds new things to the world
like ointment, it lets you see what was already there.

fork.setup: the room of your mind is dark. in the twenty-third salok, how does the darkness end?
options: you argue it away, point by point.
the Guru applies the ointment of wisdom, and it's simply gone.
you wait for it to fade on its own.
fork.reveal: gur deeaa, the Guru gave it, and agiaan andher binaas: the darkness of ignorance was destroyed, by God's grace.

original.note: Gurmukhi: anjan, eye-ointment or kohl; giaan anjan is the eye-ointment of wisdom.

trapdoor: what you thought: the guru cleared my eyes means a teacher fixed your vision.
what it means: the Guru's wisdom, given by God's grace, ends inner darkness so you see what was always there.
what a scholar hears: the salok pairs giaan with agiaan and andher with pargaas, wisdom against not-knowing and darkness against light, in two tight lines.

sources.ref: Sukhmani Sahib, ashtpadi 23, salok (Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 293)

notes: Editor review (2026-10-01): removed unsourced time claims ('for centuries', 'long believed', 'in Gurbani's day') and the 'sharpens sight' claim from the surma hook and myth; cut a stock line; the practice no longer ends 'look around as if for the first time', which day 529's see-freshly practice repeats.
Paraphrase of the ashtpadi 23 salok (giaan anjan gur deeaa agiaan andher binaas; har kirpaa te sant bhetiaa naanak man pargaas): confirm and confirm Ang 293.
Surma customs described generally as believed to cool and protect; no health claim is made.
